subject: Maths
title: Build a grouped-data report
smallprint: Bar area represents pupils; height is pupils per minute. Cumulative lines join group boundaries using constant density inside each interval, so quartile read-offs are estimates. One full grid cell represents 5 pupils, not an individual journey.
summary: Build unequal-width bars, connect their areas to cumulative totals, and estimate the middle half.
action: Set bar heights, construct cumulative totals, operate a linked read-off ruler and compare recorded distributions.
change: Frequency equals interval width times density. Cumulative growth integrates the same bar areas; quartile ranks use the same total. The learner's cumulative sketch remains a separately identified prediction until checked.
evidence: Equal-height unequal-width bars expose the area misconception. A checked cumulative sketch is overlaid with the report line; the ruler links area to rank, and an incorrect range draws a bracket that misses Q3.
decision: Revise an area rather than hunt for a green height, include all preceding groups, locate a quartile rank or compare the effect of changing a group.

frequency-density.description: Frequency divided by positive class width; actual bar area is the frequency.
frequency-density.domain: Density 0–3 pupils/min; frequency moves in whole pupils. Widths are fixed positive intervals.
frequency-density.source: Bar-top handles or a tap in the bar's plot column.
frequency-density.output: The same frequency drives filled area, cumulative totals and quartile ranks.

cumulative-frequency.description: Running total through each upper class boundary.
cumulative-frequency.domain: The guided report contains 60 pupils; the editable sketch is non-decreasing with fixed endpoints 0 and 60.
cumulative-frequency.source: Three independently editable crosses; tapping a cross column and keyboard adjustment use the same setters.
cumulative-frequency.output: Dashed learner sketch and, only after checking, the solid report line.

quartiles.description: The 25%, 50% and 75% ranks of the same grouped distribution, read on both plots.
quartiles.domain: Journey time 0–60 min; ruler increments 0.5 min. Accepted read-offs are within 0.55 pupils of the target rank.
quartiles.source: The learner moves or taps the ruler and explicitly records each estimate.
quartiles.output: Actual learner read-offs persist in working; they are not silently replaced with exact model answers.

interquartile-range.description: Difference between the learner's recorded Q3 and Q1 estimates.
interquartile-range.domain: Finite numeric or fractional minutes; tolerance 0.11 min around the difference of recorded estimates.
interquartile-range.source: A structured number entry after all three read-offs.
interquartile-range.output: A tested bracket starts at Q1 and ends at Q1 plus the entered range.

limits: A deliberately fixed, synthetic report; these are not empirical pupil measurements. No random case generator is implemented.

The original contract's bar-area and non-decreasing cumulative invariants are retained. The cumulative representation uses straight joins instead of the original smooth interpolation: constant within-class density makes partial bar area and cumulative growth agree everywhere.
The graphical cells encode five pupils of area. They do not identify individual observations or assert uniform individual journey times.
Quantiles inside grouped intervals are estimates. Empty distributions have undefined quartiles. At a plateau, the model uses the first time that reaches the rank.
Guided bars and cumulative sketches are checked only on the explicit action. Manipulation remains responsive; editing clears stale checks.

Experiment records are immutable copies, capped at six. Current and saved plots share the same axis scale without normalising counts. Repeat preserves other visited steps; restart requires explicit confirmation and clears only this lab's session.
gates: Change the second equal-width bar from frequency 10 to 20, then check both areas. The reference stays at 10.
Keep a 10-minute interval at frequency 20; reduce a 20-minute interval from frequency 40 to 20 and explicitly check. Equal heights initially imply unequal areas.
Construct frequencies 10, 20, 20 and 10 across widths 10, 10, 20 and 20 in any order, then check all bars. Matching the total alone is insufficient.
Build cumulative totals 0, 10, 30, 50 and 60 with three movable internal points, then check against the report. The sketch remains monotone even during revision.
Record Q1, median and Q3 using the linked ruler, then enter and check the range between the recorded outer quartiles. Moving a recorded read-off clears that reading and invalidates the range verdict.

Ungated experiment: alter any bar, inspect the cumulative and median consequences, save up to six frozen reports and select a comparison. Zero frequency across all intervals is valid and has undefined quartiles.
